summary: Steven Collins specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his D.Phil. at Oxford under Richard Gombrich, Margaret Cone, and Michael Carrithers, later holding posts at Bristol (~1980–1991), Indiana (~1987–1991), and Chicago (1991).

Steven Edward Lindquist is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Texas at Austin under Patrick Olivelle, also studying under traditional teachers, and held a post at Concordia University.

Steven Heine works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. Educated at the University of Pennsylvania and Temple University, and having studied under Shudo Ishii, he held appointments at Villanova, Penn State, and Florida International University (~1997).

Steven Lukes works in philosophy and other fields. After studying at Balliol College and Nuffield College, he held posts at Balliol College (~1966–1987), the European University Institute (~1987–1995), the University of Siena, LSE, and NYU (~2001).

Steven Neal Weinberger specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Amherst College and the University of Virginia, completing his PhD under Jeffrey Hopkins alongside numerous traditional teachers, and held a post at Virginia (attested 2006).

Sthaneshwar Timalsina is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies who studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and the University of Halle-Wittenberg. He held posts at Nepal Sanskrit University, San Diego State University, and Stony Brook University (~2021).

Stig Wikander was an Indologist, linguist, and Iranian-Central Asian studies scholar who studied at Uppsala and Copenhagen under Henrik Samuel Nyberg, Arthur Christensen, and Geo Widengren. He held posts at Lund (1941–1953) and Uppsala (~1953–1974).
Stuart McFarlane is a scholar in religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He held posts in the Department of Religious Studies at Lancaster University (attested 1991 and 2001).
Stuart Ray Sarbacker is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 2001 under the supervision of David M. Knipe.

Su Bai was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. After studying at Peking University (~1940–1944), he served there as Professor and Professor Emeritus in the Archaeology Department (~1988–2018).

Subhadradis Diskul worked in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the École du Louvre (~1949–1953) and later served as President of the Siam Society (~1982–1986) and Chairman of The Jim Thompson Foundation (~1987–2003).

Subhash Kak is an Indologist and historian who studied at NIT Srinagar and IIT Delhi. He has held academic posts at Imperial College London (~1975–1976), Louisiana State University (attested 2005–2008), and Jawaharlal Nehru University (~2019).

Sudhir Kakar, educated at St. Edward's School, Shimla, worked in religious studies and related fields. He served as a lecturer at Harvard (~1971–1972), professor at IIM Ahmedabad (~1972–1977), and department head at IIT Delhi (~1977–1980).

Sue Hamilton is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. She completed her D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich and Alexis Sanderson, and held a post at King's College London (attested 2001–2003).

Suk Fun Ng is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2014) under doctoral supervisors Jing Yin and Y. Karunadasa, and studied under teacher K. L. Dhammajoti.

Sukumar Sen was an Indian scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Calcutta (~1919–1923), where he later held a post (~1930–1964), and served as Secretary of the Linguistic Society of India (~1954–1964).

Sukumari Bhattacharji was an Indologist educated at the University of Calcutta and Jadavpur University. She held a post at Lady Brabourne College in 1945 and served as a teacher at Jadavpur University from 1957 to 1986.

Sulak Sivaraksa is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who studied at the University of Wales, Lampeter (~1954–1957). He served as editor for the Social Science Association of Thailand and held council and editorial roles at the Siam Society.

Sumanapala Galmangoda is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He has served as Director of the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2007, 2012) and Senior Professor at the University of Kelaniya (attested 2012).

Sumathi Ramaswamy is a historian and Indologist who studied at Delhi University, JNU, and the University of Pennsylvania. She held academic appointments at the University of Pennsylvania (~1991–2000) and the University of Michigan (~2000–2007).
